questions.question: Give two examples of how being a leader was hard for Nelson Mandela.
questions.expected_answer: He spent twenty-seven years in prison and missed most of his children's childhood. He was not allowed to go to his mother's funeral in 1968 or his son's funeral in 1969. He also had to make hard choices, such as refusing release in 1985 and starting secret talks with the government.

questions.question: Was Nelson Mandela always popular? Explain.
questions.expected_answer: No. The apartheid government called him a terrorist and banned his photograph and words. Some countries saw him as a terrorist too. Some people in his own movement were angry when he talked with the government and chose to forgive, and some white South Africans feared him.

questions.question: What did Mandela mean when he said he was not a saint, and why is it important to know that leaders are not perfect?
questions.expected_answer: He meant that he had made mistakes like everyone, but kept trying to do better. It is important because we should look at leaders honestly, praising their strengths and learning from their mistakes, and because it shows that ordinary people who are not perfect can also be leaders.
